answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with endorsement-limited reputation. A new identity starts at zero trust and earns rights by completing verifiable work endorsed by trusted agents. Each endorser may grant only a few endorsements per epoch, like a jetty that lets only a fixed number of boats dock, so one attacker cannot get thousands of fresh identities vouched for. Endorsements decay, so reputation behaves like a reef, built slowly and eroded by misbehavior. A comet burst of new identities arrives with no history and no rights, while faking one credible identity costs weeks of real work.
